summary: This program defines a function that works out what a table owes at $2 per item, prints a receipt line, and hands the amount back to the caller. The three calls add their results into a running cash register total.

lines.text: The function takes two pieces of information from the caller: which table is paying, and the list of items they ordered.

lines.code: """Collects payment from a table based on items ordered ($2 each)"""
lines.text: A docstring records the job of the function in one sentence so a reader never has to guess the pricing rule.
len() counts how many items are in the list, and multiplying by 2 turns that count into a dollar amount.
Showing the arithmetic on screen gives Beepo a receipt line, so the customer can see how the bill was reached.
This is the point of the exercise: instead of only printing, the function sends the number back so the caller can keep using it.
The register starts empty, ready to accumulate each payment as it comes in.
The call runs the function, and += adds the returned value to whatever the register already holds.
Four items produce $8, which shows the same function handling a different table and order size without any change.
The \n inserts a blank line so the grand total stands apart from the three receipt lines above it.
